title: Universal optimal tests of unknown unitary dynamics: determinant exponents and tensor stability
abstract: We study forward-query tests of an arbitrary fixed unitary channel against memoryless noise with unknown fixed input and output rotations. A Schur-Weyl reduction gives a family of optimal candidate tests, but leaves a channel-dependent minimization over partitions. We remove that minimization: the balanced partition is optimal simultaneously for every channel, every query number and every compact alternative family, even against adaptive and more general positive physical testers. A Gaussian Kraus-matrix identity and classical majorization yield the universal optimizer, exact determinant error exponents, polynomial finite-query bounds, and a sharp rank threshold for perfect detection. For qubits, the spin-flip spectrum determines all even-query errors. Using classical noncommutative-rank theory, we characterize stability of perfect detection under every tensor partner by a shrunk-subspace condition. A completely depolarizing partner of dimension d-1 destroys perfect detection whenever this condition fails. For the qutrit Werner-Holevo channel we compute exact exponents after adjoining the smallest possible partner, a depolarizing qubit, and for its tensor square. The independent unknown rotations, memoryless calls, unrestricted retained reference and enlarged global-unitary null in the tensor examples are essential.
